The skill requires grounding any visual diagnosis in the observations and metrics, then inspecting the shared prewarm and rollout keyframes before editing. The current rollout sheets are four exact replicas, not four independent policy alternatives: they show a clean, actively propelled turn into the merged wake and capture at 38.049. The assigned parent adds an important negative result absent from the current guidance: increasing posterior damping from 0.65 to 0.675 reduced force/moment RMS but badly regressed arrival, distance, energy, and power. I’m using that tradeoff, plus the inherited lag/allocation brackets, to select one genuinely new bounded axis.

The wake-visual skill now requires me to commit the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis to the optimizer notes before touching the policy. I’m selecting a single opposite-direction damping test (`0.65 → 0.625`): the only measured damping perturbation (`0.675`) preserved capture but weakened active traverse and raised joint excursion, so a small decrease is the cleanest evidence-grounded new-axis test while all lag, steering-gain, and allocation continuations are closed by negative results.

The candidate is now exactly one isolated parameter change: `tail_damping=0.625`, with every other successful anchor held fixed. I also added the durable negative damping lesson: higher damping reduced RMS load but worsened traversal, effort, crossflow, and peak excursions, so later workers should not interpret unloading alone as control improvement. I’m moving through the required contract/schema checks now; I will not run CFD.
